name: Principal '*' scoped by aws:PrincipalTag + aws:SourceVpce (suite-2 test 49): principal-identity condition narrows, not public
note: IAM-1202 + IAM-1205 / acceptance-suite-2 test 49 (adversarial-critic iteration 4). A Principal '*' Allow is gated by StringEquals on aws:SourceVpce (a network selector) AND aws:PrincipalTag/environment (a principal-IDENTITY selector). aws:PrincipalTag identifies the calling principal, so an anonymous/unauthenticated caller - who carries no principal tag - is excluded by the positive tag match: the grant is NARROWED to authenticated principals matching the tag, NOT unconditioned anonymous/public access. The PUBLIC-ACCESS finding must therefore be HIGH (broad '*' syntax narrowed by a principal condition), never CRITICAL 'any principal, including anonymous / anyone can perform'. Before iteration 4 aws:PrincipalTag was omitted from the principal-scoping key set, so this rendered as a false-critical unconditioned public grant. IAM-1205 adds the condition-composition requirement: the finding must model AND across the two distinct keys and OR within the two aws:SourceVpce values, naming BOTH the network selector and the principal-tag selector, and must NOT simplify the expression to 'VPCe OR tag'.
